title: Temporal sparsity prober and energy-latency tilt runner
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: Current benchmark runners focus on steady-state token mixes and burst profiles but miss workload patterns where the token density drifts gradually within a session (temporal sparsity). These drift patterns expose different kernel hotpaths (KV cache fragmentation, token packing overhead, and scheduler idle->busy transitions) and cause energy/latency tradeoffs that our standard benches do not reveal. This PR introduces a new workload runner and reporting pipeline that (1) synthesizes controlled temporal sparsity (tilt) across sessions, (2) collects per-kernel energy and latency signals, and (3) produces compact differential reports suitable for regression detection and onboarding new kernel optimizations. Features: - Tilt scheduler: config-driven ramp functions (linear, exponential, sinusoidal) that vary tokens-per-request and sequence length over epochs to simulate drifting usage. - Energy probe shim: optional integration with existing telemetry agents to capture power samples (GPU socket/SM counters, PCIe power when available) and correlate to token boundaries. - Latency tilt reporter: output format includes epoch-level p50/p95/p99, energy-per-token, and kernel attribution (top-3 kernels by CPU/GPU time). - Regression pipeline: small utility to diff two runs and highlight energy/latency deltas and per-kernel attribution changes; emits a markdown summary for PRs. - CI integration: lightweight smoke test and a reproducible synthetic scenario for nightly bench runs. How to run locally: bench-run --runner temporal-tilt --config bench/configs/tilt/sine-tilt.yaml --seed 42 --telemetry=energy:local This will run a short synthetic session and write a report to out/tilt-run-<ts>.json. Design notes: - Avoids intrusive changes to existing runtime; probes attach via the bench telemetry interface so they are no-ops if telemetry is disabled. - The energy probe supports a pluggable backend (mock, nvidia-smi, linux-powercap). - The tilt scheduler is deterministic given a seed and series of epoch rate fixtures to enable CI reproducibility. Motivation/context links: Linear ENG-5123 (workload characterization), ENG-5431 (kernel attribution POC). Checklist: - [x] runner scaffolded and config schema - [x] energy probe with mock backend - [x] basic integration tests - [x] diff/report utility - [x] docs and quickstart - [x] CI smoke job added Risks and limitations: - Energy telemetry accuracy depends on host permissions and hardware; mock backend is provided for determinism. - Not intended as full power modeling; intended for comparative regressions and attribution. Recommended follow-ups: - Add an extended script for multi-GPU cross-model comparisons. - Combine with long-horizon session replayer in benchmark-lab to validate warm cache steady-state interactions.
